newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Colruyt recoups initial losses on Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Colruyt recoups initial losses on Brussels bourse.

text.p: Retailer Colruyt managed to recoup most of its initial losses which had followed the publication of annual results late Thursday, while the Be-20 index extended its opening losses.

By 0900 GMT Colruyt stood just 1.29 percent lower at 17,250 francs after falling five percent at the outset, even though the company had announced 1996/1997 group net profit rose 12 percent, broadly in line with market expectations.
"Colruyt is a very good company, but...it's very expensive," one trader said. He noted that the share had risen in recent weeks on speculation over the future of its Dolmen unit.
Players had expected Colruyt to announce a sale or a bourse flotation of its Dolmen Computer Applications unit at Thursday's results presentation. But there was no news.
Colruyt is preparing to split Dolmen on July 1. It has said it might sell one of the parts at a later stage.

Royale Belge, the only Bel-20 stock to rise, added 75 francs or 0.74 percent to Thursday's 200-franc gain to stand at 10,275, still benefiting from renewed speculation that Dutch ING might be interested in buying the Belgian insurer.
"10,000 francs would be a good level for Royale Belge. It's too expensive for financial investors (now) but not for industrial players like ING," one trader added.
He said the market generally had become expensive in recent weeks, adding, "I have no problem with a correction".
By 0945 GMT the Bel-20 index stood 16.51 points or 0.70 percent lower at 2,358.30, following the trend in neighbouring markets after the Dow Jones .DJI weakened overnight.
